Most of Sections 4-5 are observations read off colour plots (figures); each bulleted observation is one remark with rigor numerical, the figures themselves are not extracted.

nodes.name: Quantum parameter q
nodes.statement: Let $q=e^{\pi ib^2}$ be the quantum parameter.

nodes.name: Variants g_b and Phi_b of the quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: It bears its name from the properties of its variants $g_b(z)$ and $\Phi_b(z)$ given by \Eq{\Phi_b(z)=g_b(e^{2\pi bz}) = \frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}-iz)},} where $Q=b+b^{-1}$ and $\zeta_b=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}(\frac{b^2+b^{-2}}{6}+\frac{1}{2})}$, such that \Eq{g_b(u)g_b(v)=g_b(u+v),} \Eq{g_b(v)g_b(u)=g_b(u)g_b(q^{-1} uv)g_b(v)} hold for the positive self-adjoint Weyl type operators $u,v$ with $uv=q^2vu$ in the case $|q|=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Defines $\Phi_b(z)=g_b(e^{2\pi bz})$ via $G_b$, with $Q=b+b^{-1}$ and $\zeta_b$, satisfying the quantum exponential and pentagon relations for Weyl-type operators.

nodes.name: Phi_b and g_b in terms of G_b
nodes.statement: \Phi_b(z)=g_b(e^{2\pi bz}) = \frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}-iz)},

nodes.name: Quantum exponential relation
nodes.statement: g_b(u)g_b(v)=g_b(u+v),
nodes.label: qexp

nodes.name: Quantum pentagon relation
nodes.statement: g_b(v)g_b(u)=g_b(u)g_b(q^{-1} uv)g_b(v)
nodes.label: qpenta

nodes.name: Pentagon relation for Heisenberg operators
nodes.statement: \Phi_b(p)\Phi_b(x)=\Phi_b(x)\Phi_b(p+x)\Phi_b(p),

nodes.name: q-binomial formula
nodes.statement: (u+v)^{it} = b\int_{\mathbb{R}+i0}\frac{G_b(ib\tau-ibt)G_b(-ib\tau)}{G_b(-ibt)}u^{i \tau}v^{i (t-\tau)} d\tau,
nodes.statement_short: q-binomial formula expressing $(u+v)^{it}$ as a contour integral of $G_b$ ratios times $u^{i\tau}v^{i(t-\tau)}$.

nodes.name: Classical limit of G_b to the Gamma function
nodes.statement: \lim_{r\longrightarrow 0} \frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b| (1-q^2)^{x-1}} = \Gamma(z),
nodes.label: Glim

nodes.name: Complex coloring method
nodes.statement: In short, given a complex valued function defined on the complex plane, we represent the function by coloring the complex plane according to the following rules. The argument of a complex value is encoded by the hue of a color (red = positive real, and then counterclockwise through yellow, green, cyan, blue and purple; cyan stands for negative real). The absolute value of the function is represented by the brightness and saturation of the color: strong colors denote points close to the origin, with black = 0, weak colors denote points with large absolute value, with white = $\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Color the plane: hue encodes the argument of $f$, brightness and saturation encode $|f|$ (black = 0, white = $\infty$).

nodes.name: Hue-saturation-brightness color function
nodes.statement: The color is defined by 3 numbers ranging from 0 to 1. In the present coding, at the point $z=x+iy$ with value $f=f(x+iy)$, they are explicitly given by \Eq{Hue[h,s,b]:=\{\frac{Arg(f)}{2\pi}, \frac{1}{1+0.3 \ln(|f|+1)}, 1-\frac{1}{1.1+5\ln(|f|+1)}\},} where $h$ stands for hue, $s$ the saturation and $b$ the brightness.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit HSB triple: hue $Arg(f)/2\pi$, saturation and brightness as logarithmic functions of $|f|$.

nodes.name: Coloring of the inverse function
nodes.statement: We also note that taking inverse amounts to flipping the brightness of the color, and taking the opposite hue along the imaginary direction.

nodes.name: Coloring of z^3
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{z3}, we observe that for $f(z)=z^3$ it has an order 3 zero, with the hue of color cycling around the point $z=0$ for 3 times.

nodes.name: Coloring of the Gamma function
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{Gamma} for $f(z)=\Gamma(z)$, we observe the phase change behavior and the exponential growth along the imaginary direction. The few bright spot at $z=-n,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ indicates the simple poles.

nodes.name: Coloring of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{zeta} for $f(z)=\zeta(z)$, we observe the existence of nontrivial zeros along the line $Re(z)=~\frac{1}{2}$, the trivial zeroes at $z=-2n,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ (where the color lines come together), the pole at $z=1$, and the limit $\displaystyle\lim_{Re(z)\longrightarrow+\infty}\zeta(z)=1$.

nodes.name: Double Zeta, double Gamma and quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: Let $\omega:=(w_1,w_2)\in \mathbb{C}^2$. The double Zeta function is defined as \Eq{\zeta_2(s,z|\omega):=\sum_{m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}(z+m_1w_1+m_2w_2)^{-s}.} The double Gamma function is defined as \Eq{\Gamma_2(z|\omega):=\exp\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial s}\zeta_2(s,z|\omega)|_{s=0}\right).} Let \Eq{\Gamma_b(x):=\Gamma_2(x|b,b^{-1}).} The quantum dilogarithm is defined as the function: \Eq{S_b(x):=\frac{\Gamma_b(x)}{\Gamma_b(Q-x)},} where $Q=b+b^{-1}$. The main object of study is the variant given by \Eq{G_b(x):=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}x(x-Q)}S_b(x).}
nodes.statement_short: Barnes double zeta and double gamma functions, $\Gamma_b$, the quantum dilogarithm $S_b=\Gamma_b(x)/\Gamma_b(Q-x)$ and its variant $G_b$.

nodes.name: Barnes double Zeta function
nodes.statement: \zeta_2(s,z|\omega):=\sum_{m_1,m_2\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}}(z+m_1w_1+m_2w_2)^{-s}.

nodes.name: Double Gamma function
nodes.statement: \Gamma_2(z|\omega):=\exp\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial s}\zeta_2(s,z|\omega)|_{s=0}\right).

nodes.name: Gamma_b
nodes.statement: \Gamma_b(x):=\Gamma_2(x|b,b^{-1}).

nodes.name: Quantum dilogarithm S_b
nodes.statement: S_b(x):=\frac{\Gamma_b(x)}{\Gamma_b(Q-x)},

nodes.name: G_b in terms of S_b
nodes.statement: G_b(x):=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}x(x-Q)}S_b(x).
nodes.label: GS

nodes.name: Integral formula for G_b
nodes.statement: For $0\leq Re(z)\leq Q$, $G_b(z)$ can be expressed as \Eq{ G_b(x)=\over[\zeta_b]\exp\left(-\int_{\Omega}\frac{e^{\pi tz}}{(e^{\pi bt}-1)(e^{\pi b^{-1} t}-1)}\frac{dt}{t}\right),} where \Eq{\zeta_b=e^{\frac{\pi i}{2}(\frac{b^2+b^{-2}}{6}+\frac{1}{2})},} and the contour goes along $\mathbb{R}$ with a small semicircle going above the pole at $t=0$. The integral converges absolutely for $0<Re(z)<Q$ and conditionally at the boundary.
conclusions: The integral converges absolutely for $0<Re(z)<Q$ and conditionally at the boundary.
nodes.statement_short: Integral representation of $G_b$ on the strip $0\le Re(z)\le Q$, absolutely convergent inside.

nodes.name: Integral formula for G_b
nodes.statement: G_b(x)=\over[\zeta_b]\exp\left(-\int_{\Omega}\frac{e^{\pi tz}}{(e^{\pi bt}-1)(e^{\pi b^{-1} t}-1)}\frac{dt}{t}\right),
nodes.label: intform

nodes.name: Zeros and poles of G_b and S_b
nodes.statement: The function $G_b$ and $S_b$ can be analytic continued to the whole complex plane as a meromorphic function, so that they have simple zeros at $z=Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ and simple poles at $z=-nb+-mb^{-1}$ for $n,m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.
conclusions: can be analytic continued to the whole complex plane as a meromorphic function
they have simple zeros at $z=Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ and simple poles at $z=-nb+-mb^{-1}$ for $n,m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$

nodes.name: Properties of the quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: Self-duality: \Eq{S_b(x)=S_{b^{-1}}(x),\;\;\;\;\;\; G_b(x)=G_{b^{-1}}(x).} Functional equations: \Eq{S_b(x+b^{\pm1})=2\sin(\pi b^{\pm1}x)S_b(x),\;\;\;\;\;\; G_b(x+b^{\pm 1})=(1-e^{2\pi ib^{\pm 1}x})G_b(x).} Reflection property: \Eq{S_b(x)S_b(Q-x)=1,\;\;\;\;\;\; G_b(x)G_b(Q-x)=e^{\pi ix(x-Q)}.} Complex conjugation: \Eq{\overline{S_b(x)}=\frac{1}{S_b(Q-\over[x])},\;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{G_b(x)}=\frac{1}{G_b(Q-\bar{x})},} in particular \Eq{\left|S_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=\left|G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=1 \mbox{ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$}.} Asymptotic properties: \Eq{G_b(x)\sim\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\bar{\zeta_b}&Im(x)\longrightarrow+\infty,\\\zeta_b e^{\pi ix(x-Q)}&Im(x)\longrightarrow-\infty,\end{array}\right.} where \Eq{\zeta_b=e^{\frac{\pi i}{4}+\frac{\pi i}{12}(b^2+b^{-2})}.} Residues: \Eq{\lim_{x\longrightarrow 0} xG_b(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi},} or more generally, \Eq{Res\frac{1}{G_b(Q+z)}=-\frac{1}{2\pi}\prod_{k=1}^n(1-q^{2k})^{-1}\prod_{l=1}^m(1-\widetilde{q}^{2l})^{-1}} at $z=nb+mb^{-1}, n,m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ and $\widetilde{q}=e^{\pi i b^{-2}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Self-duality, functional equations, reflection, complex conjugation, asymptotics and residues of $S_b$ and $G_b$.
nodes.label: asymp

nodes.name: Complex conjugation
nodes.statement: \overline{S_b(x)}=\frac{1}{S_b(Q-\over[x])},\;\;\;\;\;\; \overline{G_b(x)}=\frac{1}{G_b(Q-\bar{x})},

nodes.name: Unit modulus on the line Re(x)=Q/2
nodes.statement: \left|S_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=\left|G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)\right|=1 \mbox{ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$}.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of G_b
nodes.statement: G_b(x)\sim\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\bar{\zeta_b}&Im(x)\longrightarrow+\infty,\\\zeta_b e^{\pi ix(x-Q)}&Im(x)\longrightarrow-\infty,\end{array}\right.

nodes.name: Constant zeta_b (asymptotic form)
nodes.statement: \zeta_b=e^{\frac{\pi i}{4}+\frac{\pi i}{12}(b^2+b^{-2})}.

nodes.name: Residue of G_b at 0
nodes.statement: \lim_{x\longrightarrow 0} xG_b(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi},

nodes.name: Residues of 1/G_b
nodes.statement: Res\frac{1}{G_b(Q+z)}=-\frac{1}{2\pi}\prod_{k=1}^n(1-q^{2k})^{-1}\prod_{l=1}^m(1-\widetilde{q}^{2l})^{-1}

nodes.name: Extension of G_b by shifts of Q
nodes.statement: Using the functional equation \eqref{funceq}, the function can be extended to the whole complex plane using the integral formula \eqref{intform} by \Eq{G_b(z+nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z+(k-1)Q)}),} \Eq{G_b(z-nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z-kQ)})^{-1},} where $n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, $0\leq Re(z)\leq Q$.
nodes.statement_short: Shift formulas extend $G_b$ from the strip $0\le Re(z)\le Q$ to the whole plane.

nodes.name: Forward shift by nQ
nodes.statement: G_b(z+nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z+(k-1)Q)}),

nodes.name: Backward shift by nQ
nodes.statement: G_b(z-nQ)=G_b(x)\prod_{k=1}^n (1-e^{2\pi ib(z-kQ)})^{-1},

nodes.name: Symmetry and near-multiple poles in the graph of G_b
nodes.statement: We observe the symmetry along the axis $Re(z)=\frac{Q}{2}$, governed by the reflection properties \eqref{reflection}. Furthermore, the poles and zeros along $Im(z)=0$ are supposed to be simple, by comparing with the graph of $f(z)=z$ given in Section \ref{sec:complex}. The appearance of certain double or triple poles and zeros for the graph $b=0.7$ comes from the fact that $b^{-1}\simeq1.43\sim 2b$, hence certain multiples $nb+mb^{-1}$ will come close together. For example, $z=2b+2b^{-1}=4.257$ and $z=4b+b^{-1}=4.229$.
nodes.statement_short: Graph of $G_b$ is symmetric about $Re(z)=Q/2$; apparent double poles for $b=0.7$ arise because $b^{-1}\approx 2b$.

nodes.name: Exponential decay and growth of G_b
nodes.statement: It has exponential decay along the negative imaginary direction for $Re(z)<\frac{Q}{2}$, and exponential growth for $Re(z)>\frac{Q}{2}$. According to the asymptotic behavior from the last section, the growth is given by \Eq{|G_b(s+it)| = e^{-\pi t(2s-Q)},\;\;\;\;\;\; t\longrightarrow -\infty.} This also explains the brightness for different $b$ when $Im(z)\longrightarrow -\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Along $Im(z)\to-\infty$, $|G_b|$ decays for $Re(z)<Q/2$ and grows for $Re(z)>Q/2$ as $e^{-\pi t(2s-Q)}$.

nodes.name: Growth of |G_b| in the negative imaginary direction
nodes.statement: |G_b(s+it)| = e^{-\pi t(2s-Q)},\;\;\;\;\;\; t\longrightarrow -\infty.

nodes.name: Limit of G_b in the positive imaginary direction
nodes.statement: On the other hand, it approaches the limit $\overline{\zeta}_b = e^{\pi i(b^2+b^-2+3)/12}$ in the positive imaginary direction.

nodes.name: Phase change of G_b
nodes.statement: We observe the phase change along any given direction. In particular along $Re(z)=\frac{Q}{2}$ we do have the changes given according to $e^{\pi iz^2}$, increasing in frequency as $Im(z)\longrightarrow -\infty$.

nodes.name: Resemblance to the Riemann zeta function
nodes.statement: Finally let us note the similar shape compared with the Riemann Zeta function, which we believe is a coincidence.

nodes.name: Higher-order poles and zeros at b=1
nodes.statement: For the case $b=1$, from Figure \ref{Gx1} we observe that the successive poles and zeroes have increasing order, due to the fact that $b$ and $b^{-1}$ coincide, which creates multiple poles. The poles at $z=-n$ and the zeroes at $z=2+n$ both have order $n+1$ for $n=0,1,2,...$

nodes.name: Symmetry of S_b
nodes.statement: The graph can be made symmetric by considering $S_b(z)$ instead. The reflection properties give \Eq{S_b(z)=S_b(Q-z)^{-1},\;\;\;\;\;\; \over[S_b(z)]=S_b(\over[z]),} suggesting a full symmetry of the graph along $Re(z)=\frac{Q}{2}$ and $Im(z)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reflection properties make the graph of $S_b$ symmetric about $Re(z)=Q/2$ and $Im(z)=0$.

nodes.name: Reflection and conjugation symmetry of S_b
S_b is real on the real line
nodes.statement: Since we know that $\over[S_b(z)]=S_b(\over[z])$, we conclude that $S_b(z)$ takes real values when $z$ is real. Therefore it suffices to plot the graphs for $S_b(z)$, and the values for $G_b(z)$ just amount to a phase change by the factor $e^{\pi iz(z-Q)/2}$ (cf. \eqref{GS}).

nodes.name: Simple zeros of S_b on the real line
nodes.statement: We can clearly observe the locations of the poles and zeroes. The zeroes are simple from the fact that the values of the function should alternate in signs. For $b=0.7$, the appearance of a seemingly critical points comes from the fact that $b^{-1} = 1.429$ is quite close to $2b=1.4$ as explained before.

nodes.name: Recurring amplitude of S_b on the real line
nodes.statement: By the functional equation \eqref{funceq}, the whole graph really depends on the portion $0<x<Q$. The size of the bump governs the recurring amplitude of the graph by successive factor of 2, which comes from $2\sin(\pi b)\sin(\pi b^{-1})$ appearing in the reflection properties for $S_b(x)$. This also explains the "periodicity" of the log plot for $b=0.1$, which, in fact, has shifted by $\ln(2)$.
nodes.statement_short: By the functional equation the real graph of $S_b$ is determined by $0<x<Q$, with amplitude recurring by factors of 2.

nodes.name: One local minimum and maximum of S_b on (0,Q)
nodes.statement: The portion of the graph $0<x<Q$ has exactly one local minimum and one local maximum for all values of $b$, and they are all positive real numbers. By taking the log plot in Figure \ref{logSQx}, which essentially is the value of the integral, (we rescaled so that the endpoints at $x=0$ and $x=Q$ matches), we see immediately that the size of the bump has a symmetric exponential relation along $x=\frac{Q}{2}$.

nodes.name: Common limit along vertical lines
nodes.statement: We observe the asymptotic behavior, that as $x\longrightarrow \infty$, they all approach the complex number $\over[\zeta_b]=0.123-0.992i$.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of |G_b(ix)| and |G_b(Q+ix)|
nodes.statement: For $x\longrightarrow-\infty$, $|G_b(ix)|\longrightarrow e^{\pi Qx}$, while $|G_b(Q+ix)|\longrightarrow e^{-\pi Qx}$. The relationship of the two graphs can easily be derived from the reflection properties \eqref{reflection}.

nodes.name: Behaviour of G_b on the line Re(z)=Q/2
nodes.statement: Finally $|G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+ix)|=1$, and the asymptotic behavior for $x\longrightarrow-\infty$ is $\overline{\zeta_b}e^{-\pi i\frac{Q^2}{4}}e^{-\pi ix^2}$, hence the increase in frequency is governed by $\pi x^2$.

nodes.name: Compact quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: The analytic properties extend to the compact case, when $Im(b^2)>0$, using an infinite product expansion, which we will call it the \emph{compact quantum dilogarithm}:

nodes.name: Infinite product formula for the compact quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: \cite[Prop 5]{Sh} For $Im(b^2)>0$, we have the infinite product descripiton \Eq{G_b(z)=\bar{\zeta_b}\frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty (1-e^{2\pi ib^{-1}(x-nb^{-1})})}{\prod_{n=0}^\infty(1-e^{2\pi ib(x+nb)})}.}
nodes.label: infprod

nodes.name: Infinite product formula for G_b
nodes.statement: G_b(z)=\bar{\zeta_b}\frac{\prod_{n=1}^\infty (1-e^{2\pi ib^{-1}(x-nb^{-1})})}{\prod_{n=0}^\infty(1-e^{2\pi ib(x+nb)})}.

nodes.name: Poles and zeros of the compact quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: The location of the poles and zeroes are still the same, with poles at $-nb-mb^{-1}$, and zeroes at $Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ for $n,m=0,1,2,...$
conclusions: poles at $-nb-mb^{-1}$, and zeroes at $Q+nb+mb^{-1}$ for $n,m=0,1,2,...$

nodes.name: Fast decay and growth in the compact case
nodes.statement: We have highlighted the zeroes with black dots and poles with white dots that align nicely together. We observe that the exponential decay and growth are extremely fast, due to the asymmetry bringing in a real part for the asymptotic $e^{\pi iz(z-Q)}$, thus giving a quadratic exponential growth.

nodes.name: Separation of poles for smaller |b|
nodes.statement: We observe that the separation of the poles is stretching out with increased exponential decay/growth compared with bigger $|b|$.

nodes.name: Classical limit of G_b to the Gamma function
nodes.statement: The following limit holds for $b^2=ir\longrightarrow i0^+$ \Eq{\lim_{r\longrightarrow 0} \frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b| (1-q^2)^{x-1}} = \Gamma(z),} where $\sqrt{-i}=e^{-\frac{\pi i}{4}}$ and $-\frac{\pi}{2}<\arg(1-q^2)<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
also_stated_at: In fact it is shown in \cite{Ip1} that we have the limit given by \Eq{\lim_{r\longrightarrow 0} \frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b| (1-q^2)^{x-1}} = \Gamma(z),} where we analytic continued $b$ so that $b^2=ir$ with $r>0$ and the principal values of the complex powers are taken.
nodes.statement_short: As $b^2=ir\to i0^+$, the rescaled $G_b(bz)$ tends to the classical Gamma function $\Gamma(z)$.
nodes.label: limit

nodes.name: Modified quantum dilogarithm tilde G_b
nodes.statement: Let us demonstrate the limiting process by considering the graph of the above function \Eq{\til[G]_b(z):=\frac{G_b(bz)}{\sqrt{-i}|b| (1-q^2)^{z-1}}.}

nodes.name: tilde G_b at b=e^{pi i/4}0.7
nodes.statement: From Figure \ref{GG07}, we see that under multiplication by $b$ in the argument, the zeroes and poles are aligned with the axis. The first zero occur at $z=\frac{Q}{b}=1-\frac{1}{|b|^2}i$. Now as $|b|\longrightarrow 0$, we see that $\frac{Q}{b}$ moves downward and pushes away the zeroes and poles. It becomes clear in the graph for smaller $|b|$.

nodes.name: tilde G_b approaching Gamma for smaller |b|
nodes.statement: Now as $|b|$ becomes smaller, from Figure \ref{GG035} we see that the small area around center begins to take shape with the poles and zeroes pushed away. Further reducing $|b|$ so that $\frac{Q}{b}$ is out of plotting range, we can see immediately in Figure \ref{GG0248} that indeed the graph resembles the Gamma function $\Gamma(z)$ given in Figure \ref{Gamma}.

nodes.name: All variants are affine reparametrizations of G_b
nodes.statement: We will see below that all variants of $G_b$ amounts to shifting, scaling, taking inverses and multiplication by a constant. Hence the graphs of these variants can be obtained from those of $G_b(z)$ easily by shifting, stretching, and color phase changes.

nodes.name: Quantum exponential g_b
nodes.statement: The important function that satisfies the pentagon equation for Weyl-type operator is defined by \Eq{g_b(z)=\frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib})}.}

nodes.name: Definition of g_b
nodes.statement: g_b(z)=\frac{\over[\zeta_b]}{G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib})}.

nodes.name: Quantum exponential and pentagon relations
nodes.statement: Let $u, v$ be positive self-adjoint operators with $uv=q^2vu$, $q=e^{\pi i b^2}$. Then \Eq{g_b(u)g_b(v)=g_b(u+v),} \Eq{g_b(v)g_b(u)=g_b(u)g_b(q^{-1} uv)g_b(v).}
assumptions: $u, v$ be positive self-adjoint operators with $uv=q^2vu$
nodes.statement_short: For positive self-adjoint $u,v$ with $uv=q^2vu$, $g_b$ is a quantum exponential and satisfies the pentagon identity.

nodes.name: Graph of g_b avoids zeros and poles
nodes.statement: However, the graph of $g_b$ which carries a branch cut at $x\in(-\infty,0)$ is not particularly interesting, due to slow growth, and the fact that $-\pi < Im(\log z)<\pi$, so that \Eq{0<\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{1}{2b}<Re(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib}) < \frac{Q}{2}+\frac{1}{2b}<Q,} and hence the argument in $G_b$ never hits any zeroes or poles.
nodes.statement_short: Since $|Im(\log z)|<\pi$, the argument of $G_b$ in $g_b$ stays in the strip $(0,Q)$ and meets no zeros or poles.

nodes.name: Range of the argument of G_b in g_b
nodes.statement: 0<\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{1}{2b}<Re(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{\log z}{2\pi ib}) < \frac{Q}{2}+\frac{1}{2b}<Q,

nodes.name: Hyperbolic Gamma function
nodes.statement: Let $q=e^{\pi i\tau}$ for $Im(\tau)>0$. Then the hyperbolic Gamma function is defined by \Eq{\gamma(z):=\frac{(q^2e^{-2\pi iz};q^2)_\infty}{(e^{-2\pi iz/\tau};q^{-2/\tau^2})_\infty}.}

nodes.name: Volkov's hyperbolic Gamma function
nodes.statement: \gamma(z):=\frac{(q^2e^{-2\pi iz};q^2)_\infty}{(e^{-2\pi iz/\tau};q^{-2/\tau^2})_\infty}.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic Gamma function in terms of G_b
nodes.statement: With $\tau=b^2$, we have \Eq{\gamma(z)=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(Q-\frac{z}{b})^{-1}.}

nodes.name: gamma in terms of G_b
nodes.statement: \gamma(z)=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(Q-\frac{z}{b})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm psi
nodes.statement: Let $s_q(w)=\prod_{n=0}^\infty (1+q^{2n+1}w)$ and define \Eq{\psi(p):=\frac{s_q(e^{bp})}{s_{\til[q]}(e^{p/b})},} where $\til[q]=e^{\pi ib^{-2}}$. Then $\psi(p)$ admits the integral expansion \Eq{\psi(p):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{ip\xi/\pi}}{\sinh(b\xi)\sinh(\xi/b)}\frac{d\xi}{\xi}\right).}
nodes.statement_short: Faddeev's $\psi$ as a ratio of infinite products $s_q$, with an integral expansion.

nodes.name: Product definition of psi
nodes.statement: \psi(p):=\frac{s_q(e^{bp})}{s_{\til[q]}(e^{p/b})},

nodes.name: Integral expansion of psi
nodes.statement: \psi(p):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{ip\xi/\pi}}{\sinh(b\xi)\sinh(\xi/b)}\frac{d\xi}{\xi}\right).

nodes.name: Fock-Goncharov and Woronowicz quantum dilogarithms
nodes.statement: \Eq{\Phi^{\hbar}(z):=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{-ipz}}{\sinh(\pi p)\sinh(\pi \hbar p)}\frac{dp}{p}\right),} \Eq{V_\theta(z):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_0^\infty \log(1+x^{-\theta})\frac{dx}{x+e^{-z}}\right).}

nodes.name: Fock-Goncharov quantum dilogarithm
nodes.statement: \Phi^{\hbar}(z):=\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{-ipz}}{\sinh(\pi p)\sinh(\pi \hbar p)}\frac{dp}{p}\right),

nodes.name: Woronowicz quantum dilogarithm V_theta
nodes.statement: V_\theta(z):=\exp\left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_0^\infty \log(1+x^{-\theta})\frac{dx}{x+e^{-z}}\right).

nodes.name: Relations between quantum dilogarithm variants
nodes.statement: \Eq{V_{b^{-2}}(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(z)=g_b(e^{z})^{-1}=\zeta_bG_b\left(\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{iz}{2\pi b}\right),} \Eq{\psi(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(-bz)^{-1}=\gamma(b(Q+\frac{z}{2\pi i}))=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{iz}{2\pi})^{-1}.}
nodes.statement_short: Expresses $V_\theta$, $\Phi^\hbar$, $g_b$, $\psi$ and $\gamma$ as shifted, rescaled or inverted $G_b$.

nodes.name: V, Phi and g_b in terms of G_b
nodes.statement: V_{b^{-2}}(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(z)=g_b(e^{z})^{-1}=\zeta_bG_b\left(\frac{Q}{2}-\frac{iz}{2\pi b}\right),

nodes.name: psi in terms of G_b
nodes.statement: \psi(z)=\Phi^{b^2}(-bz)^{-1}=\gamma(b(Q+\frac{z}{2\pi i}))=\over[\zeta_b]G_b(\frac{Q}{2}+\frac{iz}{2\pi})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Ruijsenaars G function in terms of S_b
nodes.statement: Let $a_-,a_+$ be two positive real numbers. Ruijinaars's G function is defined by \Eq{G(a_+,a_-;z):=\exp\left(i\int_0^\infty \frac{dy}{y}\left(\frac{\sin 2yz}{2\sinh(a_+y)\sinh(a_-y)}-\frac{z}{a_+a_-y}\right)\right),} with $|Im(z)|<(a_++a_-)/2$ and extend meromorphically to the whole complex plane. Then \Eq{G(b,b^{-1};z)=S_b(\frac{Q}{2}-iz).}

nodes.name: Ruijsenaars G function
nodes.statement: Let $a_-,a_+$ be two positive real numbers. Ruijinaars's G function is defined by \Eq{G(a_+,a_-;z):=\exp\left(i\int_0^\infty \frac{dy}{y}\left(\frac{\sin 2yz}{2\sinh(a_+y)\sinh(a_-y)}-\frac{z}{a_+a_-y}\right)\right),} with $|Im(z)|<(a_++a_-)/2$ and extend meromorphically to the whole complex plane.

nodes.name: Ruijsenaars G function integral
nodes.statement: G(a_+,a_-;z):=\exp\left(i\int_0^\infty \frac{dy}{y}\left(\frac{\sin 2yz}{2\sinh(a_+y)\sinh(a_-y)}-\frac{z}{a_+a_-y}\right)\right),
